<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d421041d14cfc716e85e9bdd1da3d57d4eb3aa1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d40ba8ac64eef48425fea532f750370590ccfd65` — the merge of head `5fb667f29a7545c20ec7552ce36c579b6f3b8a68` into base `0d421041d14cfc716e85e9bdd1da3d57d4eb3aa1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d40ba8ac64eef48425fea532f750370590ccfd65 && git checkout d40ba8ac64eef48425fea532f750370590ccfd65
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0d421041d14cfc716e85e9bdd1da3d57d4eb3aa1 5fb667f29a7545c20ec7552ce36c579b6f3b8a68 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0d421041d14cfc716e85e9bdd1da3d57d4eb3aa1 && git merge --no-ff 5fb667f29a7545c20ec7552ce36c579b6f3b8a68

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d421041d14cfc716e85e9bdd1da3d57d4eb3aa1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0d421041d14cfc716e85e9bdd1da3d57d4eb3aa1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5fb667f29a7545c20ec7552ce36c579b6f3b8a68`
Local-runs: none

Isolated reviewer, read-only. Inputs: card #21131 (body and all 3 comments), PR #21204 body, its 10-file list, the net diff `origin/main...head` (merge-base `ebdb6f2a`; main-side drift since then on the touched paths is nil: sibling `.changeset/*` files and `packages/sdui-parser/objectui-lockstep.json` only), and the check-runs on the head. Code read on `origin/main` with `git show` / `git grep` only.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Public surface, `@objectstack/lint`**: adds `validateDashboardWidgetOptions` (function) and `DashboardWidgetOptionFinding` (type) from the package root. Additive; the finding shape (`severity` / `rule` / `where` / `path` / `message` / `hint`, path `dashboards[i].widgets[j].options`) and the `recordsOf` indexing match the sibling rules `validate-widget-bindings.ts` and `validate-dashboard-action-refs.ts`. Right.
2. **Registry entry** (`authoring-rules.ts`): `tier: 'advisory'`, `input: 'parsed'`, `commands: ALL`, `surfaces: CLI_ONLY` with a `surfaceReason`. Matches the `AuthoringRule` contract (`surfaceReason` is REQUIRED when `runtime-publish` is omitted). The advisory claim holds against the wiring test's own predicate (the function body forwards `d.severity`; no `severity: 'error'` literal). Note, not a defect: the adapter forwards the check's level verbatim, so the tier is exactly as true as the check's level; the file header already says a level change is a two-door decision, and the registry tier would be part of that decision. Right.
3. **Accept set**: unchanged. `packages/spec` is untouched; `DashboardWidgetOptionsSchema` stays `.passthrough()`; the check keeps `warning` and `unconsumed-widget-option`; no second key list exists in the diff (the adapter calls `checkDashboardWidgetOptions`, and the read set stays `CONSUMED_WIDGET_OPTION_KEYS`). The sentence "which `check:widget-option-census` derives from the spec" is substantiated: `scripts/check-widget-option-census.mjs` exists (root `package.json`) and reads `dashboard.zod.ts`. Right.
4. **Door behaviour**: `os validate`, `os build`, `os lint` gain one advisory warning class; exit codes move only under `--strict`, and both flags exist (`validate.ts:81` "Treat warnings as errors", exit at `:922`; `lint.ts:794`). `os build` has no `--strict` and the changeset claims none. The dict-form and id-less paths are pinned by the tests. In-repo producers on `origin/main`: no `*.dashboard.ts` writes widget `options` (app-crm and app-todo carry comments saying so; app-showcase's two `options: [` hits are dashboard filter option arrays, not widget options), so "zero findings, no example exit changes" is consistent with the tree. Right.
5. **`content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx`** (hand-written tree; no new page, so no `meta.json` edit owed). Each rewritten claim checked against the code: (a) every widget is dataset-bound and the render path reads only the consumed set — the check's header; (b) `stageOrder` is refused on a non-funnel type at parse — `checkDashboardWidgetStageOrder` via `.superRefine` in `dashboard.zod.ts`, so the old "parses and is never consulted" row was false; (c) a misspelled key parses (passthrough; `z.input` of a passthrough object admits extra keys) while a wrong value for a declared key is a type error — so the old "misspelling is an author-time error" sentence was false. The declared-homes table matches the schema doc comment, `WidgetColorVariantSchema`, and the dataset measure's `format` / `currency` (`dataset.zod.ts:278`, `:290`). Right. Pre-existing and untouched: the page says five declared keys while the warning's list has six (`description` sits in the consumed set as the translation pipeline's write target) — not introduced here.
6. **Transcript counts 48 to 49** in the four transcript pages on the file list (`deployment/cli.mdx`, `deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`, the `getting-started/` build walkthrough, `ui/react-pages.mdx`): `origin/main`'s registry holds 48 entries and all four transcripts print 48; a `commands: ALL` entry makes 49 on every command (`compile.ts:505` prints `registered.length`). Mechanical and gate-forced (`check:docs-transcript-drift`). Right.
7. **Finding message**: the check's verbatim text, which opens with the SDUI host-type spelling in angle brackets even at the metadata door. Cosmetic; lockstep-bound (the parser is a byte-equal port of objectui's); declared in Acceptance notes. Accepted as-is.
8. **Governed surfaces**: none in the file list (Governed Surface Queue Guard: success). Documentation Guardrails: no `references/`, `releases/` or `CHANGELOG.md` edits. Right.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/21131-dashboard-widget-options-door.md`: `'@objectstack/lint': minor`. Right. An additive export plus a new advisory rule; `packages/lint/CHANGELOG.md` lands the same class ("`os validate`, `os build` and `os lint` now emit one advisory `warning`...") under Minor Changes in 17.5.0. Not major: nothing is refused and no accept set narrows; the `--strict` exit flip is the flag's documented meaning and the changeset says so explicitly. No `@objectstack/cli` changeset is owed: no cli code changes; the printed count moves because the registry the cli reads grew.
- Changeset prose checked against the code: the read-set listing equals `CONSUMED_WIDGET_OPTION_KEYS`; the exemptions listed (no `dataset`, legacy `component`, `suppressWarnings`) are the check's own; "does not run on the Studio/REST/MCP publish path" equals `surfaces: CLI_ONLY`. Right.
- `Clause-②: yes` — on the card's claim (the governing limb), restated in the PR body and in the changeset; consistent, and right: the diff touches `content/docs/**` and `.changeset` prose and adds a public export.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev report (card comment 5935805280) declares `open_questions: []`, seven deviations and four out-of-scope findings.

- D1 (four transcript pages): necessary, mechanical, gate-forced — accepted.
- D2 (two in-place corrections in `dashboards.mdx`): both measured true above; same section, same defect class, declared in the PR body — accepted under Prime Directive #10's note-do-not-expand reading.
- D3 (the skill PR's third site) and D7 (no `Clause-②:` line on the skill PR's body) — judged in PR #21205's record.
- D4 (`git fetch --depth=1` of a fixture commit into the shared object store): a read into the object store, not a tree edit; no effect on the diff — noted.
- D5 (trailers): the three commits carry the session trailer pair and no model identifier — consistent with AGENTS.md; accepted.
- D6 (labels: assignee only, no `skip-changeset` because a changeset exists): right.
- OOS-1 — `DashboardWidgetOptionsSchema`'s doc comment still says a typo "is now an author-time type error" (`dashboard.zod.ts:245`), measured false, and that docblock lifts into the generated reference page. ESCALATED: this is the card's own class (a teaching surface misstating what happens to an `options` key), with evidence, and it has no carrier. Recommendation to the adopting seat: file it as a card for the `packages/spec` lane (one TSDoc edit plus `check:docs` regeneration) rather than leaving it to "whoever next edits that file". Not blocking: outside the claimed file surface, and the PR's own page no longer repeats the claim.
- OOS-2 — the Studio/REST/MCP door does not run the check: recorded in `surfaceReason`; the card's direction names `os validate` / `os build` only — accepted.
- OOS-3 (skill's Cartesian `series.dashArray` bullet) — judged in PR #21205's record.
- OOS-4 — angle-bracket host type in the message: accepted (lockstep).
- Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-01T16:44Z: 33 completed (31 success; 2 skipped: Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke opt-in) — `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carries `check:docs-transcript-drift` and the governed-prose gates), `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, every Type Check job and five of six Test Core shards among the green — and 1 still `in_progress` at reading time: **Test Core (5/6)**. It is reported as running, never as passed. This record judges the contract (landing pre-check ①); pre-check ② (every check green) is the owning seat's and is not met until that shard finishes green.
